sentences.nl: Vandaag oefenen we zinnen met de grammatica, van mijn online cursus #dutchgrammar les 36 en 37, over werkwoorden in combinatie met het woordje ‘te’, en de infinitief van een ander werkwoord.
sentences.en: Today we are practicing sentences with the grammar from my online course #dutchgrammar lesson 36 and 37, about verbs in combination with the word 'te', and the infinitive of another verb.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today practice we sentences with the grammar, from my online course #dutchgrammar lesson 36 and 37, about verbs in combination with the word 'to', and the infinitive of another verb.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence begins with "Vandaag" (Today), which sets the time and is followed by inversion, placing the verb "oefenen" (practice) before the subject "we" (we).  
• The phrase "met de grammatica, van mijn online cursus" (with the grammar, from my online course) shows possession and course specifics.  
• "Over werkwoorden in combinatie met het woordje ‘te’" (about verbs in combination with the word 'to') focuses on grammar topics. "Te" is often used before infinitives in Dutch.  
• Examples:  
  - "Ik probeer te leren." (I try to learn.)  
  - "Zij besloot te vertrekken." (She decided to leave.)  
  - "We hebben het plan om te reizen." (We have the plan to travel.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Morgen gaan we oefenen met zinnen uit de cursus over de verleden tijd. (Tomorrow we will practice with sentences from the course about the past tense.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Online language courses like #dutchgrammar are popular for learning Dutch, as they offer flexibility and access to structured content, especially for non-native speakers living outside the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: Anika ligt op het gras woordjes te leren.
sentences.en: Anika is lying on the grass learning words.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Anika lies on the grass words to learn.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ligt" is the third person singular form of "liggen," which translates to "lies" or "is lying" and indicates a position.  
• "Op het gras" means "on the grass," showing location with the preposition "op" (on).  
• "Woordjes te leren" uses the structure "te + infinitive," which is similar to the English "to + verb" for expressing purpose or activity.

• Examples:  
  - "Hij zit op de bank een boek te lezen." (He is sitting on the couch reading a book.)  
  - "Zij staat in de keuken te koken." (She is standing in the kitchen cooking.)  
  - "De kinderen liggen op het strand te spelen." (The children are lying on the beach playing.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Mark zit in de tuin een liedje te zingen." (Mark is sitting in the garden singing a song.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No culture note.

sentences.nl: Ik probeer hem al een tijdje te bellen.
sentences.en: I've been trying to call him for a while.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I try him already a while to call.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik probeer" (I try) is in the present tense, first-person singular.  
• "hem" (him) is the direct object pronoun.  
• "al een tijdje" means "already a while," indicating an ongoing action.  
• "te bellen" (to call) uses the infinitive form of the verb "bellen" (to call) with "te," which is used for infinitive constructions.  
• Extra examples:  
  - "Ik ben al een tijdje aan het lezen." (I have been reading for a while.)  
  - "Ze probeert het al een tijdje te begrijpen." (She has been trying to understand it for a while.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "We proberen hem al een tijdje te bereiken." (We have been trying to reach him for a while.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: Ik ken Martin goed,, maar hij is niet heel erg handig, in het versieren van vrouwen.
sentences.en: I know Martin well, but he is not very good at flirting with women.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I know Martin well, but he is not very handy, in the seducing of women.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik ken Martin goed" uses "kennen" (to know), which refers to familiarity with a person.  
• "maar hij is niet heel erg handig" shows negation ("niet") and uses "handig" (handy), which can mean skilled or adept.  
• "in het versieren van vrouwen" uses the preposition "in" combined with a gerund-like structure "het versieren" (the seducing), and "van" (of) to indicate what he is not skilled at.  
• Examples:  
  - "Ik ken haar niet goed." (I don't know her well.)  
  - "Zij is heel handig met computers." (She is very handy with computers.)  
  - "Hij is niet goed in het maken van vrienden." (He is not good at making friends.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik ken Peter goed, maar hij is niet heel erg handig met geld." (I know Peter well, but he is not very handy with money.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase "versieren van vrouwen" (seducing women) can imply a casual or playful approach to dating, often reflecting social interactions at parties or social gatherings in Dutch culture.

sentences.nl: Ik beloof Martin vandaag nog te bellen.
sentences.en: I promise to call Martin today.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I promise Martin today still to call.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "beloof" (promise) is in the present tense, indicating a current action.  
• "Te bellen" is an infinitive construction. In Dutch, when using infinitives after verbs like "beloven" (to promise), "te" is used before the infinitive.  
• The word order "vandaag nog" (today still) emphasizes that the action will be completed by the end of today.  
• Examples:  
  - "Ik probeer vandaag nog te schrijven." (I try today still to write.)  
  - "Hij belooft morgen te komen." (He promises to come tomorrow.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij besluit vanavond nog te koken." (She decides to cook tonight.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, keeping promises, especially those made about time commitments, is generally taken seriously. Being punctual and following through on promises is often seen as a sign of reliability and respect.

sentences.nl: Ik vergeet steeds vrij te vragen.
sentences.en: I keep forgetting to ask for time off.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I forget continually free to ask.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik vergeet": "Ik" is the subject pronoun "I," and "vergeet" is the present tense of "vergeten" (to forget).  
• "steeds": This adverb means "continually" or "repeatedly," indicating an ongoing action.  
• "vrij te vragen": "Vrij" means "free," and "te vragen" is the infinitive form "to ask." In Dutch, when using verbs like "vergeten" followed by another verb, you use "te" plus the infinitive.

### Extra Phrases  
• "Ik probeer steeds meer te leren." (I try to learn more and more.)  
• "Hij vergeet altijd zijn sleutels mee te nemen." (He always forgets to take his keys with him.)  
• "Wij plannen om vroeg te vertrekken." (We plan to leave early.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij vergeet vaak haar bril op te zetten." (She often forgets to put on her glasses.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch work culture, it is common to request time off well in advance. Forgetting to ask for time off might lead to scheduling conflicts or disappointment if too many colleagues are already on leave.

sentences.en: It must remain a surprise!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• It must a surprise remain!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The structure "Het moet... blijven" uses a modal verb "moet" (must) followed by an infinitive "blijven" (remain).  
• "Het" is a neutral pronoun used to refer to a general or unspecified subject.  
• "Verrassing" is a noun meaning "surprise."

Examples:  
• "Het moet geheim blijven." (It must remain a secret.)  
• "We moeten stil blijven." (We must remain quiet.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Providing surprises is a common part of Dutch celebrations such as birthdays and Sinterklaas, where keeping things a surprise is often important for the enjoyment of the event.

sentences.nl: Hoe gaat dit verder? — Komen Martin en Marieke dan eindelijk tot elkaar…, door een misverstandje? — Of gooit Gianluca roet in het eten? — Kijk de volgende keer naar ‘Heb je zin?’
sentences.en: How does this continue? — Will Martin and Marieke finally come together… due to a misunderstanding? — Or will Gianluca throw a spanner in the works? — Watch next time on ‘Are You in the Mood?’
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• How goes this further? — Come Martin and Marieke then finally to each other..., through a little misunderstanding? — Or throws Gianluca soot in the food? — Watch the next time to ‘Are you in the mood?’

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoe gaat dit verder?" uses "hoe" for "how" and "verder" as "further," indicating continuation or progression.  
• "Komen Martin en Marieke dan eindelijk tot elkaar" uses "dan eindelijk" to mean "then finally," suggesting anticipation or a long wait. "Tot elkaar" literally means "to each other," indicating a coming together.  
• "Gooit Gianluca roet in het eten" is an idiom meaning "to spoil the fun," with "roet" (soot) and "eten" (food).  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hoe gaat het met jou?" (How are you doing?)  
  - "Ze kwamen eindelijk tot een akkoord." (They finally reached an agreement.)  
  - "Hij gooide roet in het eten met zijn opmerking." (He spoiled the fun with his comment.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zal de vergadering doorgaan, of gooit iemand roet in het eten?" (Will the meeting go on, or will someone spoil the fun?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The idiom "roet in het eten gooien" reflects a common cultural expression in Dutch, similar to "throwing a wrench in the works" in English, indicating disruption or spoiling plans.

die.spelling: In Dutch, the pronoun 'die' is pronounced with a long /i/ sound, which is common for pronouns and demonstratives.
die.fast: In connected speech, 'die' may become a reduced vowel sound, especially in fast speech or informal contexts.

nederlands.fast: In rapid speech, the final /ts/ in 'nederlands' may be reduced, causing it to blend with following words.

tweede.spelling: The 'ee' in 'tweede' is a long vowel sound /eː/ followed by a schwa /ə/ at the end.
tweede.fast: In connected speech, the initial /t/ in ‘tweede’ can become less aspirated, sounding closer to [tw].

vandaag.spelling: The combination 'aa' in 'vandaag' indicates a long /aː/ sound, typical for Dutch vowels.
